SPHERICAL HARMONICS.
[146.
Similarly, if the potential of the second sphere is $\beta$, for points
within that sphere,
$$U+V^{\prime}=\beta .$$
(8)
For points outside both spheres the potential is $\Psi$, where
$$U+V=\Psi .$$
(9)
On the axis, between the centres of the spheres,
$$r+8=c .$$
(10)
Hence, differentiating with respect to $r$, and after differentiation
making $r=0$, and remembering that at the pole each of the
zonal harmonics is unity, we find
$$\left.\begin{array}{l}
A_{1} \frac{1}{a^{2}}-\frac{d V}{d s}=0, \\
A_{2} \frac{2!}{a^{3}}+\frac{d^{2} V}{d s^{2}}=0, \\
A_{m} \frac{m!}{a^{m+1}}+(-1)^{m} \frac{d^{m} V}{d s^{m}}=0,
\end{array}\right\}$$
(11)
where, after differentiation, $s$ is to be made equal to $c$.
If we perform the differentiations, and write $\alpha / c=x$ and
$b / c=y$, these equations become
$$\left.\begin{array}{r}
0=A_{1}+B x^{2}+2 B_{1} x^{2} y+3 B_{2} x^{2} y^{2}+\text { \&c. }+(n+1) B_{n} x^{2} y^{n} \\
0=A_{2}+B x^{3}+3 B_{1} x^{3} y+6 B_{2} x^{3} y^{2}+\text { \&c. }+\frac{1}{2}(n+1)(n+2) B_{n} x^{3} y^{n} \\
0=A_{m}+B x^{m+1}+(m+1) B_{1} x^{m+1} y+\frac{1}{2}(m+1)(m+2) B_{2} x^{m+1} y^{2} \\
+ \text { \&c. }+\frac{(m+n)!}{m!n!} B_{n} x^{m+1} y^{n}
\end{array}\right\}$$
(12)
By the corresponding operations for the second sphere we find,
$$\begin{array}{r}
0=B_{1}+A y^{2}+2 A_{1} x y^{2}+3 A_{2} x^{2} y^{2}+\text { \&c. }+(m+1) A_{m} x^{m} y^{2}, \\
0=B_{2}+A y^{3}+3 A_{1} x y^{3}+6 A_{2} x^{2} y^{3}+\text { \&c. }+\frac{1}{2}(m+1)(m+2) A_{m} x^{m} y^{3}, \\
\left.\begin{array}{r}
0=B_{n}+A y^{n+1}+(n+1) A_{1} x y^{n+1}+\frac{1}{2}(n+1)(n+2) A_{2} x^{2} y^{n+1}+\text { \&c. } \\
+\frac{(m+n)!}{m!n!} A_{m} x^{m} y^{n+1}
\end{array}\right\}
\end{array}$$
(13)
To determine the potentials, $a$ and $\beta$, of the two spheres we
have the equations (7) and (8), which we may now write
$$\begin{aligned}
& c a=A \frac{1}{x}+B+B_{1} y+B_{2} y^{2}+\text { \&c. }+B_{n} y^{n} \\
& c \beta=B \frac{1}{y}+A+A_{1} x+A_{2} x^{2}+\text { \&c. }+A_{m} x^{m} .
\end{aligned}$$
(14)
(15)
